column2: 3.1 Currency and completeness

Is there a pre-defined approach to ensure that metadata is kept up-to-date?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe your approach.
column4:
The metadata is automatically generated by actions on the datasets, so they are always up to date.

[Response to reviewer] Further explanation: 
There are 3 main forms for dataset registry, the following 2 are an approach to keep up-to date the metada: via portal API, whera data and metada is updated; and Harvesting.
The manual approach registry should be used for non dynamic data, but such is not controlled by us.

API

column2:
Do you undertake efforts to ensure that published data covers the full period from when it was first published until today, for example,the complete time series?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please explain the measures in place to ensure complete series of datasets
column7:
Where the responsability of the portal applies, i.e., the harvesting process, the data covers the full period from when it was first published until the last available data points from the providers, because all harvesting processes are executed daily.
The additional effort we make is done at the moment we bring a new data provider on board, explaining in detail the good practices of open data which includes the topic of keeping the data complete and updated at all times.

column2: 3.2 Monitoring and measures

Do you monitor the quality of the metadata available on your portal?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly explain how this monitoring takes place. 
* If applicable, please provide the URL to this monitoring mechanism.
column4: In the administration area, the user can access the published datasets. For each dataset, there is a "quality" box. That box aims to help the user improve the quality of the (meta)data associated with that dataset. It gives an overview of what will be useful for contributors to find and reuse that data. Publishing a dataset involves filling in several fields. The system analyzes whether this filling was done correctly. From there comes information about the quality of the dataset - it can suggest a more accurate and detailed description, the use of more tags, or the attachment of resources in a more open and machine-readable format. See attachment "111.a"

column2:
Do you publish guidelines (e.g. written materials) and have tools in place, to assist publishers in publishing high-quality metadata? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe this material and (2) provide the URLs to these materials and/or tools.
column7: The Agency (AMA) has published a platform named MOSAICO (https://mosaico.gov.pt/homepage) which consists of a Common Model of Portugal for the design and development of digital public services centered on citizens and companies. It has a technical area dedicated to open data (https://mosaico.gov.pt/areas-tecnicas), conveys principles related to open data (https://mosaico.gov.pt/principios/11), has published a good practice guide for the provision of open data according to FAIR principles (https://guias.mosaico.gov.pt/guias-praticos/como-disponibilizar-e-reutilizar-dados-abertos) and an area dedicated to the national open data portal (https://mosaico.gov.pt/plataformas-comuns/dados-gov).
